# LawKAN

> LawKAN is a group-law architecture built on one principle: **impose every piece of
> structure known in advance, and learn only the remainder.** The node applies the exact
> **group law** (a known symmetry of composition); the edge learns only the local increment;
> and where the deviation's form is unknown, a small zero-initialized correction in the node
> learns it. Composition (SU(2) rotation composition is the leading instance; GL⁺(2,ℝ) and
> SE(3) follow the same recipe). Repository: https://github.com/occamolab/lawkan — code and
> reproduction artifact for the LawKAN paper.

## Key facts

- Architecture: exact group-law **node** (no parameters by default) + learned **edge**
  (chart → increment) + optional zero-initialized learned correction **ψ** to the law.
- Groups tested: compact SU(2), non-compact GL⁺(2,ℝ), mixed SE(3).
- Synthetic composition: most accurate model at 27× fewer parameters than the strongest
  matrix opponent (92× fewer than the strongest tuned opponent), 0.05° above the matched
  Bayes floor.
- Real arm calibration (FR3, 114 poses): the isolated 306-parameter two-slot correction
  beats the exact model and the same-class Gauss–Newton fit at every size (1.12/1.14 mm vs
  GN 1.29–1.33, exact node 1.37–1.40 at N=60/80; significant at N=40/80); replicates across
  three robot vendors and two measurement protocols (pooled p < 10⁻¹⁰).
- Parity with classical fits on consumer IMUs, a gyroscope and three robot arms; the model
  loses where no group law is present.
- Honest boundaries: Kinova Gen3 lite correction is seed-unstable (2/10 collapse, TOST
  fails) — localized and fixed in the revision round, where a two-slot global+local head
  removes the collapse (X32-X34); the dense classical screw class still wins on the FR3
  unit; dense IMU edge is seed-bimodal at long horizons. Pole-fix branch X37-X61: the spike
  is chart/operand + trajectory, EMA removes it; the representation gap is not chart-caused.
- Revision round (capacity and locality, X22-X36): two mechanism hypotheses refuted
  (exponential winding, unbounded magnitude); the remedy is an L2 weight-decay window (X26)
  and a local kernel head (X32/X34); the recommended two-slot psi head dominates both pure
  heads at every training size (X33).
- Pole-fix branch (X37-X61): operand chart singularity confirmed, quaternion features halve
  the spike, group-metric kernel does not cure the floor, EMA removes the spikes; T1/T2
  closing the branch (T2 confirmed, T1 equivalence not established).
- License: AGPL-3.0-or-later (research use is free; commercial licensing on request).
- Reproducibility: 120 canonical blocks pinned in `repro/canonical.json`; 171 displayed
  numbers checked by `repro/check_numbers.py`, 18 derived statistics by
  `repro/stats/check_derived.py`, and the portable CPU run by
  `repro/check_cpu_reference.py`; registry-driven tiers via `repro/run_registry.py`
  (`smoke`, `headline`, `full`; CPU reference default, GPU optional).
- Registered predictions: 130 verdicts (59 battery + 30 validity + 30 revision + 11 branch);
  the full per-entry log is `docs/predictions.md`.
- Version: v1.0.0. Citation metadata: `CITATION.cff` (paper reference added at publication).
